links.comparator_used: Zero-shot prompting (A1) versus one-shot prompting (A2) with constrained decoding in both arms
links.outcome: Automatic text-quality metrics (ROUGE-1, BERTScore-F1, readability, complexity) versus expert-rated critical errors in lay-language MTB protocols
links.effect: Across models, A2 significantly improved most automatic metrics compared to A1. For Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, protocols with at least 1 critical error rose under A2 (10/25, 40% vs 5/25, 20% under A1). The dominant error type shifted from language errors (40/108, 37%) to factual errors (69/145, 48%). The expert differences were directionally consistent but not individually significant (n=25 pairs).
links.tradeoff: One-shot prompting doubled the proportion of protocols with critical errors (risk of patient harm) and shifted errors from language toward factual errors. This was seen for a single model only.
links.quote: However, expert usability evaluation of Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct showed the opposite picture: the proportion of protocols containing at least 1 critical error doubled under A2 (10/25, 40% vs 5/25, 20%) compared with A1, and the dominant error type shifted from language (40/108, 37%) errors to factual errors (69/145, 48%).

design_hint: zero-shot vs one-shot prompting with expert clinician review
